{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**To:** Deal Team
**From:** In-house Counsel (Customer side)
**Re:** Playbook review of Master Services Agreement — verified findings

---

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Master Services Agreement against the playbook and found it materially favourable to us. Of the nineteen rules assessed, seventeen are compliant — including the critical indemnification and IP/Customer Data provisions, which sit at or above our preferred position — and two are deviations requiring a redline.

The two open items are:

1. **Limitation of liability cap (§ 21, critical).** The cap is mutual and carries the full suite of uncapped carve-outs we want, but it is keyed to "Fees" as defined in §§ 1.5/1.6 — the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form only. That is neither twelve months of fees nor a meaningful cap (effectively USD 12,000 against, for example, USD 5,000,000 of cyber insurance), so it fails the fallback on a material term.
2. **Customer-payable liquidated damages (§ 7.7, high).** Liquidated damages of fifteen percent of annual Fees per week of invoice lateness are uncapped, open-ended and triggered by a minor breach. This is walk-away territory and fails the fallback, which permits only an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees as the sole liquidated amount.

Everything else — assignment and change of control, licence grant, termination for convenience, renewal mechanics and uplift cap, transition assistance and data return, warranties, audit, insurance, governing law and venue — meets the playbook, and the Agreement contains no exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit, minimum-commitment or MFN obligation binding us. Several provisions run in our favour (Vendor-side non-compete at § 12.4, Vendor-granted MFN at § 7.6) and are not flagged.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality and carve-outs | **Deviation** | § 21 Limitation of Liability |
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant | § 20 Indemnification |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | § 14 Intellectual Property and Deliverables |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24 Assignment and Change of Control |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity obligations binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13 Access Rights and Licence |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Compliant | § 9 Termination |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22 Audit Rights |
| Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Compliant | § 28 Governing Law and Dispute Resolution |
| Medium | MFN — Most-favoured-nation obligations burdening Customer | Compliant | § 7 Fees, Invoicing, and Taxes |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions | Compliant | § 2 Agreement Structure and Scope |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer | Compliant | § 12 Customer Responsibilities |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window | Compliant | § 8 Term and Renewal |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition assistance and data return | Compliant | § 11 Transition Assistance and Data Return |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19 Warranties |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 Insurance |

---

## Deviations and our proposed positions

**1. § 21 — Limitation of liability cap (critical).** We are content with the structure of § 21: it is mutual, mutually excludes indirect and consequential damages, treats our payment obligation as outside damages, and carves out confidentiality, data-protection and security breaches, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement as uncapped Excluded Claims (§ 21.3). Our issue is the cap basis alone. We propose recasting the mutual cap as the greater of (a) all amounts paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the event and (b) USD 1,000,000, removing reliance on the illusory "Fees"/first-Order-Form basis and leaving the remainder of § 21 intact.

**2. § 7.7 — Customer-payable liquidated damages (high).** We propose deleting the late-payment liquidated damages entirely and confirming the playbook position that Customer pays no liquidated damages or penalties. No other Customer-payable liquidated damages, penalties or minimum termination charges appear (§ 10 requires payment only for delivered work and § 27 permits termination without penalty), so deletion is the single, clean cure.

---

## Walk-away items

- **§ 7.7 late-payment liquidated damages.** Fifteen percent of annual Fees per week, uncapped and open-ended, triggered by a minor breach and capable of exceeding remaining contract value. This is walk-away territory under the playbook and must come out.

No other finding reaches walk-away. The § 21 cap is a material fallback failure but is remediable by resetting the cap basis.

---

## Noted, not redlined

For the record, so the team is not surprised later, the following sit short of ideal drafting but within the playbook and are not being raised:

- § 20.5 refund is on a straight-line three-year basis, and exclusions for our modifications, combinations or specifications are handled structurally through the "to the extent" allocation and § 20.3 rather than as an express list.
- § 13.2 extends the licence to contractors supporting our business rather than granting general sublicensing rights (a fallback-only element), and § 13.3 permits suspension on a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and cure.
- § 24.2's competitor bar is qualified by "without Customer's consent" rather than being absolute — but it remains within our control.
- § 19.2's conformance period for non-hosted software and Deliverables is ninety days rather than twelve months, and the malicious-code warranty is qualified by "intentionally introduced by Vendor".
- § 11.2's thirty-day data-return clock runs from our request (we control the trigger) and § 11.3 deletion follows our confirmation of successful return.

---

## Next steps

1. Issue the redline with two changes only — the § 21 cap reset and deletion of § 7.7 — flagged with the `[Playbook]` prefix, so Vendor sees a short and closable list.
2. Confirm with the business the twelve-month paid-or-payable run-rate under anticipated Order Forms, so we can defend the USD 1,000,000 floor as proportionate to exposure and to Vendor's USD 5,000,000 cyber cover under § 18.
3. Hold the § 7.7 deletion as non-negotiable; if Vendor presses for a late-payment remedy, the playbook fallback tolerates only an early-termination fee capped at three months' Fees as the sole liquidated amount, and we should note that § 9.1 already gives Vendor an uncured-material-breach termination right.
4. Once the two items are resolved, we have no further playbook objections and can clear the Agreement for signature."}
